title: LLM prefetch + routing ideas (scratchpad)
content:
Personal scratchpad for prefetch + routing feature ideas. Rough PRD outline, user stories, acceptance criteria, and open questions. Notes to self - very rough.

Problem / motivation:
- Many product routes (chat, qna, summarization) have high repetition in opening prompts / context. For longer sessions, KV cache helps but cold-starts + short sessions still pay full token cost.
- We can reduce per-token cost and latency by prefetching likely KV prefixes and routing requests to cheaper model variants when quality tradeoff is acceptable.
- Want a lightweight experiment to measure unit-economics impact and UX regressions.

Proposal (high level):
- Add a user-configurable prefetch layer that can precompute KV cache for common prefixes (templates, system prompts, first-turn context) and store per-route short-lived prefetched entries.
- Combine with routing policy that maps requests to model variants based on route, latency SLO, and quality budget.
- Default strategy: for recognized child routes (e.g., support-chat-v1), try prefetched small-KV on cheap model (quantized) for first 2 turns; fallback to full model on mismatch/failure.

Goals (what success looks like):
- 15-30% reduction in token spend for chat-like routes under realistic traffic mixes.
- No more than 5% user-visible quality regressions on monitored evaluation prompts.
- Latency improvement for cold-starts (first token) by 20-40ms on average.

Non-goals:
- Not building full semantic caching or retrieval augmented generation (RAG) - this is about LLM KV prefetch + routing, not data retrieval.
- Not supporting unlimited long-lived caches in MVP.

User personas / owners:
- Product engineers who manage per-route perf/cost (primary).
- Platform SREs (observability/rollback).
- Enterprise customers who need predictable unit economics (later).

Rough feature components (implementation sketch):
1) Prefetch config at route level (console + API):
   - prefix patterns to prefetch (literal templates, route tags)
   - TTL for prefetched KV (short - e.g., 1m, 5m)
   - target model variant for serving prefetched entries
2) Prefetch service / queue:
   - background job that compiles small sequences and stores KV blobs indexed by route+prefix fingerprint
   - lightweight storage with LRU eviction (in-memory + optional Redis for Dedicated)
3) Routing policy engine extension:
   - policy rules: prefer_prefetch, prefer_low_cost_variant, require_full_model
   - health checks / quality monitors to automatically disable prefetched routing when regressions detected
4) Observability + evals:
   - route-level metrics: prefetched_hit_rate, prefetched_miss_cost_saving, prefetched_quality_delta
   - sampled logs for human review (which route hits prefetch, examples where fallback occurred)

User stories (examples):
- As a product engineer, I want to enable prefetch for the support-chat route so that new sessions show faster first-response latency and lower cost.
- As an SRE, I want automatic rollback if quality delta exceeds threshold to avoid degrading customer experience.
- As a developer, I want to see per-route cost impact and a per-prompt example where the prefetched path changed the output.

Acceptance criteria / experiments:
- Feature flagged rollouts: enable for 1% traffic -> 10% -> 50% with canary evaluation.
- Automated eval harness: run 2k prompts through prefetched path vs baseline; compute ROUGE/embedding-similarity and flag regressions >5%.
- Measure cost: token-equivalent cost saved per 1k sessions; show ROI over a month for typical chat route.

Open questions / risks:
- How to fingerprint prefixes robustly? (exact match vs template extraction vs fuzzy match).
- Billing implications: do we bill prefetched tokens? internal accounting? Need finance input.
- Memory pressure in Dedicated/private deployments - need config knobs and optional external KV store integration.
- Fallthrough semantics: when prefetch hits but output deviates, do we synchronously recompute on full model (adds latency) or return prefetched result and log for later?
- Security: avoid prefetching user-specific private data inadvertently. Prefetch must respect PII rules and per-customer isolation.

Metrics to track (initial):
- Prefetch hit rate (per route)
- Average first-token latency improvement
- Token spend delta per route
- Quality delta (embedding-sim similarity + custom evals)
- Fallback rate (prefetch->full model)

Rollout plan (very rough):
- Phase 0: internal experiment with synthetic traffic + eval harness (eng-serving-runtime + applied-ml).
- Phase 1: opt-in beta for internal Redwood apps (console, internal chat).
- Phase 2: gated beta for customers via console toggle + API flags.

Engineering notes / implementation rough tasks:
- Runtime: expose API to load prefetched KV for a request fingerprint; runtime should accept optional kv hint and validate kv version. (serving-runtime changes + small protocol extension)
- Console: route-level toggles, metrics dashboard for hit rate and quality. (console-and-rollouts)
- Dedicated/private: add config to store prefetched KV in configured Redis/HSM-backed store and TTL controls.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Sync with Ethan (SRE) on eviction strategy - schedule meeting.
- Create JIRA spike for fingerprinting approaches (JIRA-7890 referenced).
- Build small PoC: prefetch for 3 most common support-chat templates; run 10k synthetic sessions and collect metrics.
- Draft short Confluence page summarizing design and expected tradeoffs.

Notes to self / TODO phrasing:
- Keep the prefetch TTL conservative at first (30s-2m).
- Focus on short fixed prefixes (system prompts + welcome messages) for initial wins.
- Coordinate with billing team before wide rollout (which tokens are charged?).

Examples / quick sketches: (handy quick prompts)
- support-chat route example: system: "You are Redwood support assistant..." user: "Hi, I have an issue with my billing" => prefetch KV for system prompt + known opening Qs.
- summarization route: prefetch standard instruction templates for TL;DR mode.

End of scratchpad. 
(leave as draft - will iterate into a PRD once we pick fingerprint strategy and get buy-in from SRE/finance)
